questions.question:
The base (or radix) of the number system such that the following equation holds is_______.
[latex]\frac{312}{20}=13.1[/latex]
questions.explanation:
In base b: [latex]312=3b^2+b+2[/latex], [latex]20=2b[/latex], [latex]13.1=b+3+\frac1b[/latex].
[latex]3b^2+b+2=2b\left(b+3+\frac1b\right)=2b^2+6b+2\Rightarrow b^2=5b\Rightarrow b=5[/latex]

Answer: 5

questions.question:
Given f(w,x,y,z) = [latex]\sum_{m}[/latex]
  (0,1,2,3,7,8,10) + [latex]\sum_{d}[/latex]
  (5,6,11,15), where d represents the don't care
condition in Karnaugh maps. Which of the following is a minimum product-of-sums (POS)
form of f(w,x,y,z) ?
questions.explanation:
The zeros of f are minterms 4, 9, 12, 13, 14 (5, 6, 11, 15 are don't-cares).
- [latex](\bar w+\bar z)[/latex] is 0 when w = z = 1: covers 9, 13 (and don't-cares 11, 15)
- [latex](\bar x+z)[/latex] is 0 when x = 1, z = 0: covers 4, 12, 14 (and don't-care 6)

Together they cover every 0 and no 1.

Answer: [latex](\bar w+\bar z)(\bar x+z)[/latex]

questions.question: If the numerical value of a 2-byte unsigned integer on a little endian computer is 255 more than that on a big endian computer, which of the following choices represent(s) the unsigned integer on a little endian computer?
questions.explanation:
Write the little-endian value as [latex]256h+l[/latex] (high byte h, low byte l). The same bytes read big-endian give [latex]256l+h[/latex].

Difference [latex]=255(h-l)=255\Rightarrow h=l+1[/latex].
- 0x6665: h = 0x66, l = 0x65 True
- 0x0100: h = 1, l = 0 True
- 0x0001 and 0x4243 have h = l [latex]-[/latex] 1 False

Answer: 0x6665 and 0x0100

questions.question:
Consider 4-variable functions [latex] f 1, f 2, f 3, f 4 [/latex] expressed in sum-of-minterms form as given below.
[latex] \begin{aligned} & f 1=\sum(0,2,3,5,7,8,11,13) \\ & f 2=\sum(1,3,5,7,11,13,15) \\ & f 3=\sum(0,1,4,11) \\ & f 4=\sum(0,2,6,13) \end{aligned} [/latex]


With respect to the circuit given above, which of the following options is/are CORRECT?
questions.explanation:
Compute the AND, OR and XOR outputs as minterm sets:
- AND: [latex]f_1\cdot f_2[/latex] = common minterms = [latex]\{3,5,7,11,13\}[/latex]
- OR: [latex]f_3+f_4=\{0,1,4,11\}\cup\{0,2,6,13\}=\{0,1,2,4,6,11,13\}[/latex]
- XOR keeps minterms present in exactly one of them: [latex]\{3,5,7\}\cup\{0,1,2,4,6\}[/latex]; 11 and 13 are in both, so they drop.

[latex]Y=\Sigma(0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7)=\Pi(8,9,10,11,12,13,14,15)[/latex] (i.e. [latex]Y=\bar A[/latex]).

Answer: [latex]Y=\Sigma(0,\ldots,7)[/latex] and [latex]Y=\Pi(8,\ldots,15)[/latex]

questions.question:
Consider the following Boolean expression.

[latex]F=(X+Y+Z)(\overline X +Y)(\overline Y +Z)[/latex]

Which of the following Boolean expressions is/are equivalent to [latex]\overline F[/latex] (complement of [latex]F[/latex])?
questions.explanation:
Find where F = 1 (XYZ): X = 1 forces Y = 1 (second factor), Y = 1 forces Z = 1 (third), and 000 fails the first. So [latex]F=\Sigma(1,3,7)[/latex] and [latex]\overline F=\Sigma(0,2,4,5,6)[/latex].

- [latex]X\bar Y+\bar Z[/latex] = {4, 5} [latex]\cup[/latex] {0, 2, 4, 6} = {0, 2, 4, 5, 6} True
- [latex](X+\bar Z)(\bar Y+\bar Z)[/latex] = {0, 2, 4, 5, 6} True
- [latex]X\bar Y+Y\bar Z+\bar X\bar Y\bar Z[/latex] = {4, 5} [latex]\cup[/latex] {2, 6} [latex]\cup[/latex] {0} True
- Option 1 is the dual, not the complement (it contains 1, not 0) False

Answer: Options 2, 3 and 4
